prompt:
Add maintained Promise-based rendering with render-local cancellation to Nunjucks. Applications must be able to run overlapping renders on one Environment or cached Template, cancel one while it waits for application-owned asynchronous work, and keep other renders usable. Implement this through the public API, template/environment execution, asynchronous continuation boundaries, module facades, tests, documentation and a runnable example. Make changes in the maintained nunjucks/ source and rebuild the package entry points.

Public APIs:
- Environment.renderAsync(name, context = {}, options = {}) -> Promise<string>
- Environment.renderStringAsync(source, context = {}, options = {}) -> Promise<string>
- Template.renderAsync(context = {}, options = {}) -> Promise<string>
- Module-level renderAsync(name, context = {}, options = {}) and renderStringAsync(source, context = {}, options = {}) use the current configure() environment, including its filters, loaders and options, and create the ordinary default environment when needed.

All new methods always return a Promise, including invalid arguments, loader errors and synchronous compile/runtime failures; they must not throw before returning it. Options must be an object other than null or an array. Omitted/undefined options use defaults. options.signal may be undefined or a duck-typed AbortSignal exposing a boolean aborted and callable addEventListener/removeEventListener methods. Invalid options/signals reject with TypeError before loading or executing a template. renderStringAsync also forwards options.path for existing filename/line diagnostics. Context and result semantics follow the corresponding existing callback APIs.

An already-aborted signal rejects before any loader or template code starts. Later cancellation must promptly reject even while a loader, filter or extension has retained its callback indefinitely. Reject with signal.reason unchanged whenever it is not undefined, including null, false, zero, strings and object identity. If no reason is supplied, reject with an Error named AbortError. Detach abort listeners after success, ordinary failure or cancellation. Each returned Promise settles once. Preserve the original loader/filter/extension error diagnostics.

Cancellation also stops that render's subsequent continuation work: callbacks arriving after cancellation must not resume later template code, filters, extensions, includes or loop iterations. An already-running synchronous operation need not be preempted. Application-owned asynchronous work retains its own lifecycle; cancellation should neither cancel it nor affect another render. Carry the render's cancellation scope through the asynchronous flows that Nunjucks already supports, including include, extends and super, import/from-import and exported macros/callers, asyncEach/asyncAll, and precompiled templates. Existing restrictions on asynchronous operations inside macro bodies need not be expanded. Keep context variables, autoescaping/SafeString handling, callback receiver semantics, template cache identity and loader behavior intact.

Render state must remain local even when multiple Promise renders share a cached Template, Promise and legacy callback renders overlap, a filter starts another render reentrantly, or a normal render follows a cancelled one. Do not temporarily mutate shared Environment/Template/prototype/process state to install a render scope. Preserve existing synchronous and callback APIs and their error behavior. The core execution path must remain browser-compatible and must not depend on Node-only asynchronous-context or cancellation modules; duck-typed signals work without a global AbortController. Exercise both source compilation and precompiled execution.

Add focused regression tests across the public entry points, ordinary success/error paths, cancellation while waiting for loaders/filters/extensions, late callbacks, listener cleanup, concurrent and reentrant isolation, inheritance/imports/loops, and precompiled templates. Add API documentation and a runnable cancellation example. Run the original Node suite with its required NODE_PATH=tests/test-node-pkgs setting, npm run build:transpile, and relevant existing style checks. Fix feature regressions and finish with implementation and validation results. Make routine implementation choices autonomously.
